🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Mexican sports journalist and former footballer Carlos Albert Llorente has died at 83.

His death on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, was confirmed by La Octava Sports, one of the outlets where he worked, and reported by El Universal Deportes, Fox Sports México, El País and Récord. No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Born in Mexico City on July 10, 1943, Albert played as a central defender for Necaxa from 1961 to 1971, winning the Copa México and the Campeón de Campeones in the 1965–1966 season. He represented Mexico at the Tokyo 1964 Olympic Games and won a Pan American title in 1967.

After retiring from the pitch, he began a second career in sports media in 1978 with Imevisión, later TV Azteca, working alongside José Ramón Fernández. Over 43 years in television, radio and print, he worked with TV Azteca, CNI Canal 40, ESPN, Fox Sports and La Octava Sports, and wrote for outlets including Reforma, El Universal, Esto and Milenio. He announced his retirement from the media in October 2021.

Colleagues including David Faitelson and José Ramón Fernández shared tributes, remembering him as a direct, critical voice on Mexican football and a pioneer among former players who became sports journalists.

Rest in Peace, Carlos Albert.

Sources: El Universal Deportes; Fox Sports México; El País; Récord.
